items: Engineering precision: The assessment of a machine’s design is an engineering process aimed at confirming that the machine is safe, functional and compliant with legal requirements (e.g. the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC).
Broad perspective: The assessment covers not only the machine itself, but also its intended use and potential operator errors.
Practical verification: The design assessment does not end on paper. It requires physical testing of the prototype, as well as technical trials (operation under load, functionality checks).

blocks.text: Here are the reasons why we carry out machine design assessments:

For a machine to be legally placed on the market (particularly in the EU), it must comply with the requirements of the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC (or the newer Regulation 2023/1230) and harmonised standards. The design assessment is part of the procedure for obtaining the CE mark.
The assessment helps implement the safety hierarchy: first, safe design; then, technical measures (guards); and finally, informing the user of the risks.
The aim is to analyse and eliminate the risk of accidents, injury or breakdowns by introducing appropriate protective measures, guards or control systems.
Verifying the design before production allows errors to be detected, which, if rectified at the finished machine stage, is significantly more expensive and time-consuming.
Structural analysis includes strength calculations, material selection, and diagnostics of vibration and noise sources, ensuring longer and trouble-free operation.
The assessment checks whether the design ensures comfortable, safe working conditions and reduces operator strain.
